To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the statistical approaches based on a direct model for the raw data or on multiple imputation of the raw data are the best suited to the analysis of the motivating data.

(1) multiple imputation applied directly to the raw data is a powerful approach to analyse longitudinal data, even in the presence of missing values and (2) the influence of subjects on parameter estimates should be taken into account by individual estimations given in the model

(i) the choice of statistical approach depends on the assumptions about the missingness mechanism and on the constraints imposed by the data analysis; (ii) the use of appropriate statistical models can be useful to describe the influence of subjects who have incomplete profiles; (iii) multiple imputation applied on the raw data is particularly well adapted to the context of summarization of longitudinal data at landmarks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of longitudinal data that have been summarized at scheduled landmarks.
the analysis of longitudinal data collected at scheduled times.
the analysis of longitudinal data collected at regular intervals in the context of a clinical trial.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the study are not significantly different from those obtained with a placebo, and that the compound is not effective in reducing the pain in subjects suffering from the disease.
the results of the analysis based on multiple imputations of the raw data are the most robust and should be preferred to those of the other statistical approaches.

multiple imputation applied at the raw data level, using a specific dropout mechanism, is a particularly appropriate approach for analysing intensive longitudinal pain data in the context of a clinical trial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice of statistical approach depends on the type of inferences required and the assumptions that are appropriate for the missingness mechanism.

the choice of the statistical approach for inferences should be based on the missingness mechanism and the model assumptions, and that the choice of a statistical method for missing data imputations should not be based solely on the type of the data (i.e. continuous, binary, etc.).
, in this context, the use of multiple imputation for longitudinal profiles with missing values is particularly well adapted to the data structure and the dropout mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful choice of the statistical approaches to be used in the analysis of intensive longitudinal data after summary at landmarks is essential.

, in the context of intensive longitudinal data after summary, the use of multiple imputation applied on the raw data can be a powerful approach to make inferences about the population mean of the outcome and the individual effect of a covariate.
the statistical analysis of longitudinal data should be guided by the missingness mechanism.
